summary.value: The Empordanesa is a Spanish chicken from the Emporda area of Catalonia, in the far northeast of the country. It is a Mediterranean laying breed that copes well with hot weather. Its best known feature is the egg, which ranges from a warm reddish terracotta to a deep chocolate brown, far darker than most brown eggs. Hens lay roughly 160 to 180 eggs a year, and improved lines can reach about 220, with each egg weighing around 60 grams. Reported sizes vary: roosters weigh from about 5.5 to 7.5 pounds and hens from about 4 to 5.5 pounds. The comb is unusual. It starts as a normal single comb in front but splits into several points at the back, so it looks like a small crown. Red, white, buff and partridge colors are kept. The breed nearly vanished in the twentieth century and was rebuilt from farm flocks starting in 1982.
